newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union says to launch strike on Friday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union says to launch strike on Friday.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions said on Tuesday it would launch an all-out strike on Friday unless a controversial new labour law was repealed.
"We plan an all-out strike on Friday to deter the new law from taking effect from March 1," said a leader of the confederation.
The confederation earlier said it would decide when to order its member unions to walk out after a televised address by President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday.

Kim apologised over the labour law rammed through parliament last December, but fell short of satisfying the union, which demanded the revoke of the law that makes it easier for employers to lay off workers and replace strikers.
President Kim also apologised for a loan scandal which followed the financial collapse of Hanbo Steel.
Hanbo collapsed late in January after racking up $5.8 billion in dubious loans.
Union leaders said they would also look for more positive results from parliamentary debates which reopened last week.
Ruling and oppostion parties are discussing possible revision of the law in a labour committee.
The confederation's earlier plan to go on strike on February 18 was postponed to February 24-28 as it wanted to see how parliament would handle the revision of the new labour law.
The National Assembly reopened on February 17 for a 30-day session to discuss the labour law and probe into the Hanbo scandal.
The ruling New Korea party passed the law in parliament in late December while opposition members were sleeping, triggering almost a month of strikes.
